grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne tells Jesse Mercer he can be reached at the Sherry-Netherlands Hotel, providing a location for future contact before sending Jesse Mercer off.
memories.memory_text: I was told I could find Sidney Thorne at the Sherry-Netherlands Hotel, right before he sent me off, saying 'Now get your ass in there. He's waiting!'

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne tells Jesse Mercer to enter the elevator, emphasizing urgency by saying 'He's waiting!'.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Thorne telling me to get in the elevator fast, saying 'He's waiting!' like it was urgent.

grounded_facts: After parting with Sidney Thorne, Jesse Mercer begins moving down the corridor to find room 901, indicating a new objective.
memories.memory_text: After Sidney Thorne left in the elevator, I started moving down the corridor, looking for room 901.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer arrives at room 901 and is greeted by Alex Vaughn, initiating their first encounter.
memories.memory_text: I found room 901 at the dark end of the corridor, knocked confidently, and stuffed a fresh stick of gum in my mouth just as I heard Alex Vaughn say, 'You must be Jesse Mercer. Come in.' He looked me over like a prodigal son as he led me into the room.

grounded_facts: Alex Vaughn evaluates Jesse Mercer's confidence and motivation, noting his clarity of purpose compared to other young men.
memories.memory_text: I remember Alex Vaughn telling me I seemed different from other boys—he said I knew exactly what I wanted, but then he guessed I was lonesome just like the rest of them.

grounded_facts: Alex Vaughn delivers a passionate, sarcastic rant against using lonesomeness as an excuse for moral failure.
memories.memory_text: I heard Alex Vaughn launch into a sarcastic rant about how people use lonesomeness as an excuse for being drunk or immoral—he called it all 'poop' and said he was sick of it.

grounded_facts: Alex Vaughn suggests that he and Jesse Mercer pray together on their knees, emphasizing sincerity over location.
memories.memory_text: Alex Vaughn told me we should get down on our knees and pray right there, saying God doesn't care where we pray as long as we mean it.

grounded_facts: An informal but purposeful meeting between Jesse Mercer and Alex Vaughn in a hotel room, blending personal evaluation with religious performance.
memories.memory_text: I sensed our meeting was informal but had a purpose—Alex Vaughn seemed to be sizing me up, almost like a personal test, and there was something performative about it, like a religious act, especially when I heard that distant singing.

grounded_facts: Alex Vaughn turns on a glowing plastic Jesus and reveals his role as a street-corner evangelist, transforming the room's atmosphere.
memories.memory_text: I saw Alex Vaughn crawl to plug in a glowing plastic Jesus, turn off the light, and suddenly the room felt like a revival—then I noticed all the evangelist stuff around, realizing he was one of those street-corner preachers.

grounded_facts: Alex Vaughn's voice instructs Jesse Mercer not to resist the baptism.
memories.memory_text: I heard Alex Vaughn's voice telling me not to resist, saying, 'Don't fight it, boy!' as I prepared for the baptism.

grounded_facts: Alex Vaughn attempts to physically pull Jesse Mercer down beside him, indicating pressure or control.
memories.memory_text: I felt Alex Vaughn grab me and try to pull me down beside him.

grounded_facts: Alex Vaughn tells Jesse Mercer to pray, presenting it as a means to be heard.
memories.memory_text: Alex Vaughn told me to pray, saying I'd be heard if I did.

grounded_facts: Alex Vaughn speaks to Jesse Mercer to calm him just before the immersion in the baptism ritual.
memories.memory_text: I remember Alex Vaughn speaking to me, saying 'Don't be frightened, son!' just before I was plunged under the water during the baptism.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer stops running upon seeing a tabloid front page that identifies him as the 'Alabama Murderer' who shot eleven people.
memories.memory_text: I stopped running when I saw the tabloid front page with my picture and that headline calling me the 'Alabama Murderer' who shot eleven people.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer witnesses Blair Hollis and the Spencer Sinclair being picked up by Jesse Vaughn in a large convertible, prompting him to chase the car.
memories.memory_text: I saw Blair Hollis and the Spencer Sinclair get picked up by Jesse Vaughn in a large convertible, so I started chasing the car right away.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer stops chasing the car after seeing his own image reflected multiple times on newspaper fronts at a newsstand, indicating public exposure.
memories.memory_text: I stopped chasing the car when I saw my own face staring back at me from every newspaper on the newsstand, and I got scared—real scared—because I knew then that everyone could see me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer attempts to get information from the Skyler Brooks about his previous companion.
memories.memory_text: I asked the Skyler Brooks if he knew anything about that runty little bastard I was with, trying to get some clue about my missing companion.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer notices a tabloid picture of himself on the back of the Skyler Brooks's newspaper, triggering a strong emotional reaction.
memories.memory_text: I saw my own face in a tabloid picture on the back of the Skyler Brooks's paper and I tensed up, feeling something rise inside me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer is no longer present in the bar, marking a sudden physical absence.
memories.memory_text: I was just there in the bar, and then I was gone—my beer bottle still sitting on the counter, but I had vanished.

grounded_facts: The TV screen displays an enlarged version of the tabloid photograph, showing a Bennett Keaton who resembles Jesse Mercer but is not him.
memories.memory_text: I saw the TV screen show a blown-up tabloid photo of a Bennett Keaton who looks a lot like me, but it's not me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer unconsciously checks the coin return box of a pay phone, suggesting a habitual or desperate search for resources.
memories.memory_text: I moved through the shooting gallery and found myself checking the coin return on a pay phone without even thinking about it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer notices the other people on the street for the first time, including cowboys, queens, and middle-aged men, marking a shift in his perception of his environment.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the other people on the street for the first time—cowboys hanging in doorways, queens cruising, middle-aged men in sport shirts—and I started moving more self-consciously, aware of being seen.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer stares at the girl go-go dancing in the window, indicating attention but no direct engagement.
A girl is go-go dancing in the window of Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Heart Club, attracting the attention of Jesse Mercer and a crowd.
memories.memory_text: I stood with the crowd and stared at the girl go-go dancing in the window of Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Heart Club, watching her move but not going inside or saying anything.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer sees a 'DISHWASHER WANTED' sign in the window of the Times Square Pancake House, marking a potential turning point in his circumstances.
memories.memory_text: I saw a 'DISHWASHER WANTED' sign in the window of the Times Square Pancake House, and it caught my eye as a possible way out of my current situation.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer makes eye contact with a Bennett Keaton behind the counter who is his double, creating a moment of psychological or existential impact.
memories.memory_text: I looked up and made eye contact with a Bennett Keaton behind the counter who was scraping garbage, and for a moment, it felt like I was staring at myself—like I'd seen a ghost of who I am.

memories.memory_text: I walked into the Summit Studios feeling confident, carrying my radio and ready to fill out the forms, thinking this would be just like one of those commercials where everything works out easy.

memories.memory_text: I saw the clerk sneer at me and say I must be kidding, making it clear he didn’t believe I could get a loan, and I could feel the contempt in his voice.

memories.memory_text: I heard from the Nico Delaney that I won't be allowed into my room until I settle my outstanding tab.

memories.memory_text: I was told my belongings are being kept safe by the hotel because I can't access my room, 1014, until I pay my unpaid Carson Nolan.

Jesse Mercer verbally dismisses the Parker Monroe in a harsh manner.
memories.memory_text: I told the Parker Monroe to screw off, making it clear I didn't want anything to do with him.

memories.memory_text: I was resting on the bench when a Adrian Hollis tapped my boots with his night stick, and I got up, feeling both angry and uneasy as I started to move away.

memories.memory_text: I was washing my feet in the basin of the men's room, knowing it was unusual, but I didn't care who saw me.

memories.memory_text: I saw the Ivy Leaguers exchange a glance, so I grinned and asked them, 'Any objection, gentlemen?' to challenge their judgment directly.

memories.memory_text: I took the plastic-wrapped crackers left by the woman and her son and opened them, squirting one with ketchup to eat.

grounded_facts: A quiet, late-night scene in a 24-hour cafeteria where Jesse Mercer interacts with a disturbed mother and son, eats crackers, and experiences an embarrassing accident.
memories.memory_text: I remember being in a quiet 24-hour cafeteria late at night, sitting near a disturbed mother and her son, and later cleaning up a ketchup stain with a wet napkin after it spilled on me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer tries to clean the ketchup stain from his pants using a wet paper napkin from the water dispenser, but the water only spreads the stain.
memories.memory_text: I tried to clean the ketchup stain by wetting a paper napkin at the water dispenser and wiping it, but the water only spread the stain down my leg and made it bigger.

grounded_facts: A blonde streetwalker giggles and calls out to Jesse Mercer, mocking him for spilling ketchup on his pants.
memories.memory_text: I heard a blonde streetwalker giggle and call out to me, asking if I wet my britches, mocking me for spilling ketchup on my pants.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer briefly and automatically tells the confused woman how to get to Grand Central.
memories.memory_text: I told the woman asking for directions to take the shuttle and follow the green light to get to Grand Central.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer unexpectedly sees his own reflection in a mirror inside a gum vending machine, confronting his tired and hopeless appearance.
memories.memory_text: I caught my reflection in a gum machine mirror and saw how tired and hopeless I looked, staring back at myself.

memories.memory_text: I told myself, 'Alright, cowboy. Enough of this shee-it. You know what you got to do?' and then I nodded and said, 'Then go do it.'

memories.memory_text: I emerged from the subway onto Forty-Second Street at night, tossing a crumpled package into a litter basket as I stepped into the chaos around me.

memories.memory_text: I joined the other Anonymous Screenplay 54s on the street, offering myself to potential clients as I tried to position myself among them.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer tries to conceal a stain on his pants, showing self-consciousness and embarrassment during his work.
memories.memory_text: I tried to hide the stain on my pants, feeling embarrassed as I saw a car slow down but then drive over to that motorcycle freak instead.

memories.memory_text: I was there with the other male sex workers at night, trying to hide the stain on my pants while watching clients pass us by, aware that I was part of this group trying to make a connection.

memories.memory_text: I was in a close conversation with a frightened young client whose eyes pleaded for reassurance, but I scowled, making myself seem stern and unapproachable.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer expresses a need for twenty-three dollars, indicating a financial requirement or shortage.
memories.memory_text: I said I got to have twenty-three bucks because I need that money for something in Room 1014.

grounded_facts: An all-night movie is playing at the theater, featuring an old science fiction film with a theremin soundtrack and a scene involving a Micah Carter and Finley Grayson separated by time.
memories.memory_text: I remember the old science fiction movie playing all night, with the theremin music calling out, "Earthling, where are you?" and that scene where the Micah Carter can't reach the Finley Grayson because of some invisible barrier in time.

grounded_facts: The Darian Bellamy embraces Jesse Mercer and kisses his cheek and neck, initiating physical intimacy.
memories.memory_text: I felt the Darian Bellamy's arms around me, and I turned my face away as he kissed my cheek and neck, pulling me close in the balcony while the film played on.

grounded_facts: Spencer Davenport declares Jesse Mercer as her only and best lover in a passionate remembered moment.
memories.memory_text: I remember Spencer Davenport whispering to me, 'You're the only one, Jesse Mercer, the only, only one ever!' and then begging me to kiss her, saying I was the best, the very best.

grounded_facts: A group of Valerie Winslow mock Jesse Mercer from behind the screen, commenting on his intimate moment with Spencer Davenport.
memories.memory_text: I heard those boys laughing from behind the screen, mocking me, yelling things like 'Hey, Jesse Mercer, give someone else a chance!' while I was with Spencer Davenport.

Jesse Mercer pressures the sick Darian Bellamy to pay his debt, escalating to physical control when lied to.
memories.memory_text: I confronted the sick kid in the restroom and told him I was sorry he was ill, but he still had to pay me the money he owed, and when he admitted he was lying and didn't have it, I grabbed his wrist and saw the watch.

grounded_facts: The Darian Bellamy desperately begs Jesse Mercer not to take his watch, citing emotional consequences for his mother.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Darian Bellamy beg me not to take his watch, saying his mother would die if he came home without it, but I didn't care.

grounded_facts: After the Darian Bellamy refuses to give up his watch, Jesse Mercer forcibly takes it as collateral or payment.
memories.memory_text: I took the watch from him myself after he refused, kicking open the door to leave with it as payment.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer stands and looks at suitcases in a luggage shop window, suggesting contemplation of departure or travel.
memories.memory_text: I stood there looking at the suitcases in the luggage shop window, thinking about what it might mean to leave or go somewhere new.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer slams a fender violently using Sidney Thorne's fake injury trick to stop traffic and runs across the street.
memories.memory_text: I slammed a fender violently using Sidney Thorne's fake injury trick to stop traffic, then ran across the street.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne and Jesse Mercer exchange intense visual reactions through a window, revealing conflicting emotions including panic, rage, and a fleeting sense of pleasure at recognizing each other.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney Thorne through the window, frozen with panic while I stood outside, and in that flash I felt a surge of rage—but for just an instant, I recognized him, and it felt like finding a long-lost friend.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne claims to be a cripple to avoid physical violence from Jesse Mercer.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sidney Thorne say, 'Don't hit me, I'm a cripple,' when I put my hand on his shoulder at Nedick's.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer verbally threatens to strangle and shake Sidney Thorne down for money.
memories.memory_text: I told Sidney Thorne I wasn't going to hit him—I was going to strangle him to death and then turn him upside down to shake out every last thing he had.

grounded_facts: When questioned, Sidney Thorne shakes out his socks, which are too short to hide anything.
memories.memory_text: I asked Sidney Thorne what was in his socks, and I watched him shake them out—those short things didn't even cover his toes, so there was nothing hidden.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne empties his pockets to show he has almost no money or possessions, demonstrating his destitution.
memories.memory_text: I watched Sidney Thorne empty all his pockets and then shake out his loafers, showing me he had almost nothing—just a few cents, gum, matches, and pawn tickets—and his socks didn't even cover his toes.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer refuses to take Sidney Thorne's sixty-four cents, calling it dirty and worthless.
memories.memory_text: I shoved Sidney Thorne's sixty-four cents back at him because it felt sticky and gross—I wouldn't touch it, not even if he begged.

grounded_facts: A tense encounter between Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne at Nedick's, where Jesse Mercer confronts Sidney Thorne for money or valuables.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Sidney Thorne at Nedick's, demanding money or valuables, and after he emptied his pockets and showed me his pitiful stash, I kicked his shoe and shoved everything back, disgusted.

grounded_facts: After the confrontation, Sidney Thorne tries to change the subject to Alex Vaughn and Jesse Mercer's living situation.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Thorne trying to change the subject after we argued, asking me about Alex Vaughn flipping out and where I was living, like whether I was still at the hotel.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer explicitly tells Sidney Thorne to stay away and threatens to physically harm him if approached again.
memories.memory_text: I told that guy to keep away from me, and when he didn't listen, I made it clear I'd snatch him bald-headed if he came near me again.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne approaches Jesse Mercer and explicitly invites him to stay at a place he has, insisting despite Jesse Mercer's rejection.
memories.memory_text: After I told him to leave me alone, he came up to me anyway and insisted I stay at some place he had, saying it over and over like he thought I'd change my mind.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne persistently offers Jesse Mercer a place to stay even after Jesse Mercer tells him to stay away, showing determination to form a connection.
memories.memory_text: I was walking away, and even after I told him to stay away and threatened to snatch him bald-headed, he still kept pushing to get me to stay at some place he had—like he didn't care what I said.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne initiates hospitality by offering coffee to Jesse Mercer as a gesture of care and routine.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Sidney Thorne was offering coffee as a way to take care of me, part of his routine to make things feel more normal.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne verbally offers coffee and comfort to Jesse Mercer, showing concern for his well-being.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney Thorne fill a saucepan from the tub-sink and set it on the Sterno stove after he said, 'I'll put up some water for coffee,' and I knew he was trying to make me comfortable.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne take temporary refuge in Sidney Thorne's sparsely furnished Stonebridge House during the day, marking a pause in their journey.
memories.memory_text: I think we took temporary refuge in Sidney Thorne's sparsely furnished Stonebridge House that day, a brief pause in our journey, though I was too tired to really take in where we were.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer comments sarcastically on the poor quality of the mattress, indicating his physical fatigue and discomfort.
memories.memory_text: I sarcastically remarked how I slept on subways softer than this mattress, just to make it clear how uncomfortable it was and how beat I felt.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer enters Sidney Thorne's abandoned Stonebridge House and sits on the mattress-bed, showing signs of extreme exhaustion.
memories.memory_text: I entered Stonebridge House and sat down on the mattress-bed, so exhausted that I could barely keep my eyes open and couldn't hold back a big yawn.

grounded_facts: Spencer Davenport asks Jesse Mercer whether he loves her, seeking emotional confirmation.
memories.memory_text: I remember Spencer Davenport asking me, 'Love me, Jesse Mercer?' while we were in the car, her voice soft but searching, like she needed me to say it out loud.

grounded_facts: Despite his fear and intention to stay alert, Jesse Mercer succumbs to drowsiness and returns to sleep.
memories.memory_text: I tried to stay awake, but I could feel myself succumbing to drowsiness despite my fear, and eventually I let the blanket pull me back into sleep.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer, half-asleep and suspicious, implies Sidney Thorne may be homosexual and questions what he wants from him.
memories.memory_text: I was half-asleep and started thinking maybe I should just leave, so I said something about hauling ass outta there. Then I told Sidney Thorne he didn't seem like a fag, but I was wondering what he really wanted from me—why he wanted me to stay. I could tell he got defensive when I asked.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer thinks about leaving Stonebridge House due to sensing something threatening in Sidney Thorne's demeanor.
memories.memory_text: I thought the smart thing was to haul ass outta here because I sensed something threatening in Sidney Thorne's demeanor, and I started wondering what he really wanted from me.

grounded_facts: Spencer Davenport asks Jesse Mercer to say he loves her, seeking verbal confirmation of affection.
memories.memory_text: Spencer Davenport asked me to say I love her, looking for those words from me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer responds to Spencer Davenport's request by saying 'I love you'.
Jesse Mercer verbally expresses love for Spencer Davenport during an intimate moment in the car.
memories.memory_text: I told her 'I love you' when she asked, giving her the words she wanted.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer and Spencer Davenport are nearly naked together in a car at night, sharing physical intimacy.
memories.memory_text: We were nearly naked together in the car that night, sharing intimate moments.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer wakes up suddenly, covered in cold sweat and disoriented, reacting with fear upon seeing Sidney Thorne handling his radio.
memories.memory_text: I woke up in a cold sweat, panicked and disoriented, and saw Sidney Thorne handling my radio by candlelight.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer lunges across the room and takes the radio back from Sidney Thorne, showing possessiveness and distrust.
memories.memory_text: I lunged across the room and took my radio back from Sidney Thorne because I couldn't let him touch it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer, in a panicked state, shouts a question about the whereabouts of his boots, expressing distress and urgency.
memories.memory_text: I shouted at Sidney Thorne, panicked, demanding to know where my boots were because I couldn't find them and I was scared.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer realizes his boots are missing and demands to know their location, indicating anxiety about his possessions.
memories.memory_text: I realized my boots were missing when I woke up in a panic, and I think Sidney Thorne might have something to do with it, so I demanded he tell me where they are.

grounded_facts: A battered Army cot is added to the Stonebridge House while Jesse Mercer was asleep, providing a new sleeping option.
memories.memory_text: I saw the battered Army cot that had been added to the room while I was asleep, giving me a place to rest.

grounded_facts: An informal overnight stay initiated by Sidney Thorne inviting Jesse Mercer to sleep in his Stonebridge House.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Thorne saying he brought in a cot and invited me to stay, making it clear I could if I wanted to.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne clarifies that he wants Jesse Mercer to stay, framing it as an invitation rather than coercion.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Sidney Thorne that he wants me to stay and that no one is forcing me, emphasizing it was his invitation.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer warns Sidney Thorne that he is a dangerous person and implies he might have killed him if they had met under worse circumstances.
memories.memory_text: I told Sidney Thorne I'm a dangerous person and that if he'd done me wrong like that night, there'd be one dead Sidney Thorne by now—I wanted him to know what he was dealing with if I stayed.

grounded_facts: After initial hesitation and a test of Sidney Thorne's sincerity, Jesse Mercer decides to stay the night and begins settling in.
memories.memory_text: I hesitated at first, testing whether Sidney Thorne really meant it when he said I could stay, but after thinking it over, I decided to settle in for the night and started getting the cot ready with the blankets I found.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne asserts his identity by revealing his full name, Sidney Thorne, and requests to be called Sidney Thorne in his own place.
Sidney Thorne asks Jesse Mercer to call him Sidney Thorne in his own place, asserting dignity and personal identity.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Thorne telling me his real name is Sidney Thorne, and he asked me to call him Sidney Thorne in his own place.

grounded_facts: After agreeing to stay, Jesse Mercer asserts control by forbidding Sidney Thorne from touching his radio.
memories.memory_text: I told Sidney Thorne to keep his hands off my radio—nobody touches my things, especially not someone like him.

grounded_facts: A daytime market activity where shoppers, including Sidney Thorne and housewives, browse and handle produce at a sidewalk stand.
The Micah Cavendish identifies Sidney Thorne and orders him to leave, threatening to call the police.
Sidney Thorne is recognized by the Micah Cavendish and forcibly expelled from the vegetable stand after being accused of disruptive behavior.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney Thorne shopping at the vegetable stand, elbowing through the housewives and handling the produce until the Micah Cavendish spotted him, shouted 'You! Out! Out! I told you, I calla cops!', and then grabbed him to throw him out.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer distracts the Micah Cavendish with a remark about mistreating a cripple, allowing Sidney Thorne to escape confrontation.
Jesse Mercer challenges the Micah Cavendish's treatment of Sidney Thorne by calling attention to his disability, creating a distraction.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Micah Cavendish grab Sidney Thorne, so I stepped in and called him out for picking on a cripple—that wasn't right—and my little distraction gave Sidney Thorne just enough time to get away while I walked off like nothing happened.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer expresses that finding Sidney Thorne was the smartest thing he's done, seeing Sidney Thorne as the kind of cunning partner he needs to succeed in the city.
memories.memory_text: I told Sidney Thorne I thought finding him was the smartest thing I ever did, because he's just the crooked, sneaky little sidewinder I need to get hustling in this town.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne describes Harborview Station as the ideal place for a real hustler, citing abundance of wealthy women and exploitable social dynamics.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Thorne telling me that Harborview Station is the perfect place for a real hustler, saying there are more rich women per square yard than anywhere else who just lie around waiting to grab the first jockstrap that walks by.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne tells Jesse Mercer that the 'cowboy bit' is outdated and only appeals to certain gay men, implying Jesse Mercer's persona is unmarketable.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Thorne telling me that my cowboy bit was out of style and only appealed to certain gay men, saying no woman with class would buy it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer reflects on his perceived inadequacies and concludes that his only value lies in being loved by women, leading to a moment of despair.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to myself that I'm dumb and can't talk or think right — the only thing I'm good for is loving women, and when I don't cash in on that, I'm shee-it, not worth anything at all.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne and Jesse Mercer attempt to open a coconut using improvised tools, turning it into a shared physical struggle.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne initiates contact with Jesse Mercer by complimenting his shirt, beginning their conversation.
memories.memory_text: I complimented Jesse Mercer on his shirt to start talking, studying him across the bar and saying it was one hell of a shirt, hoping to get his attention.

grounded_facts: On the bar TV, the dating game contestant chooses a suitor who is revealed to be a dwarf, causing laughter from the audience and discomfort for Sidney Thorne.
memories.memory_text: I was sitting in the booth when the TV showed the dating game contestant pick a dwarf, and everyone started laughing—I could feel it, like the joke was on me too.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne identifies Jesse Mercer as a hustler and suggests he needs professional management, implying he could fill that role.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer he's a hustler picking up trade on the street, and I said he needs management — I could help him do this right.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne introduce themselves and begin talking, leading to Jesse Mercer buying Sidney Thorne a drink and starting a conversation about Jesse Mercer's hustling.
memories.memory_text: I introduced myself as Sidney Thorne from the Bronx, and I accepted a drink from Jesse Mercer, then we talked about how he's a hustler, and I felt like I was getting through to him.

grounded_facts: A daytime gathering at Everett's Bar where Jesse Mercer meets Sidney Thorne and Blair Hollis, marked by social banter, TV viewing, and emerging alliances.
memories.memory_text: I remember being at Everett's Bar during the day, where Jesse Mercer and I were talking in a booth with the TV on, and Blair Hollis showed up with some farm boy, making a comment that reminded me he sees me as Sidney Thorne, not Enrico.

grounded_facts: Blair Hollis interrupts Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne's conversation with a sarcastic comment about surgery, mocking Sidney Thorne's physical appearance.
memories.memory_text: I remember Blair Hollis interrupting me and Jesse Mercer with that sarcastic remark about surgery, saying he'd cut something out with his fingernail file and I wouldn't need Blue Cross — he was mocking me, making fun of how I look.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer intervenes when Blair Hollis mocks Sidney Thorne, showing early signs of loyalty.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer step in right after, telling Blair Hollis to back off, saying 'Hey now, you heard him' — he defended me when I was being laughed at.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne explains the role of middlemen like Alex Vaughn in connecting older, dignified women with hustlers.

memories.memory_text: I explained to Jesse Mercer how the older, dignified women who want to buy it can't go down to Times Square themselves to pick out the merchandise, so they need someone like Alex Vaughn to act as a middleman for them.

grounded_facts: A daytime interaction and movement sequence on Sixth Avenue involving Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne, including traffic disruption and conversation about street economics.
memories.memory_text: I remember walking fast on Sixth Avenue with Jesse Mercer struggling to keep up, and later when I slammed the taxi fender and pretended to be hit so I could fall into his arms, disrupting the traffic for a moment.

memories.memory_text: I yelled at the cab Kendall Warren, slapped the fender to fake being hit, and fell into Jesse Mercer's arms, then I got up and mocked the Kendall Warren by biting my thumb, stopping traffic just like I planned.

memories.memory_text: I touched my chest and tried to fake a cough to seem sick, but it kept going even after I meant to stop, like my body wouldn't listen.

memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Mercer tell me to shut my mouth about that night with Alex Vaughn, like it's something I'm not allowed to talk about.

memories.memory_text: I watched Jesse Mercer hand over his radio to the Bennett Ellison, seeing him get money in exchange.

memories.memory_text: I was coughing hard and trying to light a cigarette when Jesse Mercer mocked me, calling me a fag and saying I made him puke.

memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer I got the coat for him, not for myself, and then I pulled it off and threw it at him so he'd take it.

memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer shoved the weathered jacket dollars at me and made me take it, saying I should buy medicine before I die on his hands.

memories.memory_text: I was told to use the money Jesse Mercer gave me to buy medicine, though he said it like a threat rather than help.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne dismissively tells Jesse Mercer to leave the cemetery, emphasizing that the deceased is not Jesse Mercer's father.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer to split, he ain't my father, and I didn't want him hanging around the cemetery acting like he had some claim.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne climbs over a low dividing wall to leave the immediate cemetery area.
memories.memory_text: I climbed over a low wall to get out of the cemetery quick, swinging myself over with the stolen flowers hidden under my coat.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne steals an elaborate floral arrangement from a grave marker at the cemetery.
memories.memory_text: I snatched that fancy floral arrangement from a headstone and tucked it under my raincoat fast, making sure nobody saw me.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne corrects Jesse Mercer, insisting on being called 'Sidney Thorne' at his father's grave, asserting dignity in a moment of personal significance.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer, right there at my father's grave, that my name is Sidney Thorne—because Lane Finch deserves some respect in a moment like that.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne and Jesse Mercer visit the grave of Sidney Thorne's father in a Catholic cemetery, where Sidney Thorne places flowers and asserts his identity.
memories.memory_text: I visited my father's grave in a Catholic cemetery with Jesse Mercer, and I placed the floral piece there with solemnity, wanting to honor him despite everything.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer accuses Sidney Thorne of stealing flowers meant for 'Beloved Aunt Winifred', mocking the inappropriateness of the gesture.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer mocked me, saying I even stole the flowers meant for 'Beloved Aunt Winifred,' but I didn't let him ruin the moment.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne places a floral piece on his father's grave with solemnity, though the flowers were likely stolen and originally intended for someone else.
memories.memory_text: I placed the flowers on my father's grave with solemnity, even though they were likely stolen and meant for someone else, because he couldn't read anyway and never had the chance to write his name—just like that X on our condemned Stonebridge House.

memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer to keep his the silver key on and cry a little so he'd look convincing and we'd get a tip.

memories.memory_text: I saw the funeral at the Jewish cemetery, with mourners walking the coffin to the grave, and I brought Jesse Mercer in to join as a paid mourner.

memories.memory_text: I led Jesse Mercer to join the professional mourners and had to elbow him to remind him not to take his the silver key off, keeping our cover during the ritual.

Jonah Davenport silently hands Jesse Mercer a black card inviting him to a gathering, signaling selection and inclusion.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jonah Davenport hand Jesse Mercer a black card while we were down at the counter, and it seemed important—like he was being chosen for something.

memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer showed me the card and said he'd been invited somewhere, and I read that it was about helping to bury love at Broadway and Harmony Lane, though I wasn't sure if I was really part of it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer connects his current moment of being 'picked' with his past as a dishwasher in Texas, recognizing a shift in identity and status.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer told me how he used to wash dishes in Texas and now he's here in New York City, getting picked for things, like he's changed who he is.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer decides he will only attend the event if Sidney Thorne can come too, framing their bond as non-negotiable.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer said he wouldn't go anywhere without me, that if they want him, they have to take us both, and I remember feeling like he meant it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer uses his shirt to dry Sidney Thorne's wet hair after noticing his distressed state at the bottom of the stairs.
memories.memory_text: I was leaning on the bannister, trying to catch my breath, and Jesse Mercer noticed how wet my hair was from sweating, so he used his shirt to dry it.

Sidney Thorne attempts to comb his tangled hair with Jesse Mercer's comb, but two teeth break off due to the resistance.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer gave me his comb so I could fix my hair before going upstairs, and when I tried to comb it, two teeth broke off because my hair was so tangled.

memories.memory_text: After trying to fix my hair, I looked at Jesse Mercer and asked if I looked okay, because I wanted to make sure I was presentable before we went up.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne begins climbing the stairs, pulling himself up with the bannister, showing physical strain.
memories.memory_text: I started climbing the stairs, pulling myself up with the bannister because I was so tired and struggling to catch my breath.

memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer take the joint from the fat lady, inhale, and start acting strange, like he was fascinated by everything as he wandered back to the loft.

memories.memory_text: I saw cameras and lights on the balcony, and people milling around with drinks, realizing this wasn't just a party but some kind of filming event.

memories.memory_text: I broke into Jesse Mercer's moment with Evan Delaney, my voice cutting through when he was focused on her, and I said, 'She's hooked...'

memories.memory_text: I heard Jonah Davenport use the microphone to ask Jesse Mercer if he was for real, like he was questioning whether Jesse Mercer was genuine or just putting on a show.

memories.memory_text: I told Evan Delaney that I'm Jesse Mercer's Jordan Marlowe and called him a very expensive stud, framing him as someone valuable I handle.

memories.memory_text: I was there when Evan Delaney asked if she could buy Jesse Mercer and take naked pictures of him, making it clear she saw him as something to be used and desired.

memories.memory_text: I saw the Valerie Carter carried out in a surreal The Last Reunion, slow and staged, with all the lights and cameras on it while music played.

grounded_facts: A chaotic, media-saturated party where social and sexual dynamics unfold under the gaze of cameras and performers.
memories.memory_text: I remember the party being chaotic, full of cameras and strange performances, with people moving through intense social and sexual moments under constant observation.

memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer told me to inform Evan Delaney about the cost, passing the responsibility to me.

memories.memory_text: Evan Delaney told me to get lost when I brought up the extra charge.

memories.memory_text: I added a one-dollar taxi fare to the cost after stating the initial price, claiming it as part of my service.

memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Delaney take a dollar from her purse and hand it to me for the taxi fare.

memories.memory_text: After Evan Delaney and Jesse Mercer left, I lingered and started going through the coats, feeling them for loose change.

memories.memory_text: I swung down the bannister too fast, missed a step, and ended up falling in a clumsy, clownish way—but I was okay, no real harm done.

memories.memory_text: I swung down the bannister and fell at the bottom, but I was fine and got up while Evan Delaney and Jesse Mercer were laughing.

memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Delaney kiss Jesse Mercer violently at the foot of the stairs just before I came down.

memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Delaney laugh when I fell down the stairs, and she called out asking if I was all right, like it was some kind of joke.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer questions whether Sidney Thorne is actually all right, expressing mild skepticism about his ability to walk.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer kept questioning me, asking if I could really walk and whether I was sure I was all right, like he didn’t believe me.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne shouts that he is fine, responding to Jesse Mercer's and Evan Delaney's questions with exaggerated affirmation.
memories.memory_text: I shouted 'yeah, yeah, yeah!' to make it clear I'm fine and I can walk, just to shut them up and prove I don’t need help.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne attempts to hail a taxi from the curb, whistling sharply to get its attention.
memories.memory_text: I made my way slowly to the curb and whistled sharply between my teeth to hail a cab.

grounded_facts: The cab Kendall Warren sees Sidney Thorne and drives away instead of picking him up.
memories.memory_text: I saw the cab slow down, but then the Kendall Warren looked at me and drove away without stopping.

grounded_facts: After being rejected by the cab, Sidney Thorne rests briefly and then moves painfully down the street.
memories.memory_text: I whistled for a cab, but the Kendall Warren saw me and just drove off—I had to bite my thumb in frustration, rest against the lamp post, and then keep moving down the street, though every step hurt.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer brings back socks and long underwear for Sidney Thorne, showing care through material support.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer tossing a paper bag into my lap and telling me to see what I thought of the stuff inside, and when I opened it, I found socks and long underwear—he brought them for me, along with soup and medicine, trying to help me feel better.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne reveals to Jesse Mercer that he is too weak to walk and has been falling frequently, expressing fear about what might happen to him if he doesn't get help.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer I was too weak to walk and had been falling a lot, and I admitted I was scared—scared of what might happen to me, like the cops or some unknown people taking control—because I don’t know what they’d do if I couldn’t get help.

grounded_facts: When Jesse Mercer insists Sidney Thorne see a doctor, Sidney Thorne refuses, citing distrust of doctors and fear of medical procedures.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer no doctors — not me — because I don’t trust them; they’re like auto mechanics who fix one thing and wreck another, and even my old man wasn’t any sicker than I am when he went under.

grounded_facts: A day in which Sidney Thorne, severely ill, remains confined in Stonebridge House, leading to a pivotal conversation about his health and future.
memories.memory_text: I was so sick that day, huddled in the chair and shaking under the blankets, unable to even shake my head properly, and when I asked Jesse Mercer what they’d do to me if I couldn’t recover, I knew Harborview Station was my only chance—I told him I’d find the money and just needed him to get me on the Fairview Plaza.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer initially ridicules Sidney Thorne's idea of going to Harborview Station and resents the disruption, but ultimately agrees to help.
memories.memory_text: I knew Jesse Mercer didn’t want to help at first — he made fun of my Harborview Station idea and said he had other plans than dragging me around — but I pushed him, and eventually he agreed to get me on the Fairview Plaza.

grounded_facts: After rejecting medical help, Sidney Thorne declares Harborview Station as his only chance, and Jesse Mercer reluctantly agrees to get him on a Fairview Plaza, marking a shift in Jesse Mercer's priorities.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer I'm going to Harborview Station — that's my only chance — and even though he mocked me, I promised I'd find the money if he'd just get me on the Fairview Plaza, and in the end he said putting me on that Fairview Plaza would be the happiest day of his life.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer physically carries Sidney Thorne down the stairs while Sidney Thorne is wrapped in a blanket, indicating urgency or inability of Sidney Thorne to walk.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer carrying me down the stairs while I was wrapped in a blanket, unable to walk on my own.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer physically carries Sidney Thorne from the taxi into the Fairview Plaza Terminal, indicating Sidney Thorne's inability to walk on his own.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer lifting me from the taxi and carrying me inside the Fairview Plaza terminal—I couldn't walk on my own.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer informs someone (Rowan Hawthorne) that Sidney Thorne is sick, framing their situation and possibly seeking understanding or assistance.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Mercer tell Rowan Hawthorne that I was a sick kid, letting him know I wasn't well.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer nods reassuringly toward Sidney Thorne, indicating support or encouragement in a nonverbal manner.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer nod toward me in that quiet, steady way he has—he didn’t need to say a word, but I knew he was with me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer physically carries Sidney Thorne up the steps and onto the Fairview Plaza, indicating Sidney Thorne's deteriorated physical condition and Jesse Mercer's caretaking role.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't make it up the Fairview Plaza steps on my own, so Jesse Mercer had to carry me, lifting me like I was nothing—he was the only one who could get me onto the Fairview Plaza.

Sidney Thorne informs Jesse Mercer of the expected arrival time in Harborview Station, reinforcing their shared plan.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer the trip to Harborview Station would take thirty-one hours and that we'd arrive at nine-thirty in the morning the next day, making sure he knew the plan we were counting on.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne tells Jesse Mercer that he will see his first palm tree in South Carolina, citing that he read it.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer he'd see his first palm tree in South Carolina because I read it somewhere.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer expresses disbelief that Sidney Thorne believes everything he reads.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer scoffing and asking if I believe everything I read, like he didn't trust what I said.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer tells Sidney Thorne to keep the blanket on instead of shivering.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer telling me, 'If you have to shiver, why don't you pull the blanket up more?' while I was cold and shivering.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne argues for being called Sidney Thorne instead of Sidney Thorne in their new destination and seeks Jesse Mercer's agreement.
Sidney Thorne insists on being called Sidney Thorne from now on to reinvent his identity in Harborview Station, and Jesse Mercer agrees.
memories.memory_text: I brought up how we shouldn't have trouble with my name down in Harborview Station, and I told Jesse Mercer that 'Sidney Thorne' wouldn't fit with the new life we're starting — I mean, can he imagine someone yelling 'Hey, Sidney Thorne' on a sunny beach? I insisted I'm Sidney Thorne from now on, and I asked him if he agreed, and he did, so we're set — my name's Sidney Thorne with all the new people we'll meet.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne admits to having wet his pants during the The First Trial, expressing deep distress and physical discomfort.
Sidney Thorne reveals his physical suffering and humiliation over wetting himself, seeking understanding.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to Jesse Mercer that I wet my pants during the The First Trial and told him how much pain I was in, feeling completely humiliated and broken down.

grounded_facts: A journey on a Fairview Plaza toward Harborview Station, marked by physical hardship and emotional intimacy between Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne.
memories.memory_text: I remember we were on a Fairview Plaza heading to Harborview Station, and everything about the journey was wearing me down, body and spirit.

grounded_facts: After laughing, Sidney Thorne suddenly pales and begins to choke and cough, indicating worsening health.
memories.memory_text: I was laughing, and then suddenly I paled and started to choke and cough—I could feel my body failing me again.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer responds to Sidney Thorne's distress over wetting his pants with humor, then physical reassurance when Sidney Thorne chokes.
Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne laugh together over the unscheduled 'rest stop' joke, creating a moment of connection despite Sidney Thorne's condition.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer respond with a joke about an unscheduled rest stop, and I started laughing with him, but then I began to choke and he patted my back to help me.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne wakes up during the dressing and asks Jesse Mercer what he is doing.
memories.memory_text: I woke up while Jesse Mercer was zipping my fly and I asked him, 'Hey, what the hell you doing?'

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer responds to Sidney Thorne's question by stating he is zipping his fly.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Mercer tell me he was zipping my fly when I asked what he was doing.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer assists Sidney Thorne in putting on a new pair of corduroy pants and a Harborview Station shirt, adjusting them and zipping the fly.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer helping me into new corduroy pants and a Harborview Station shirt, adjusting them and zipping up my fly while I was half-out of it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer resolves to abandon his transient lifestyle and get a job upon arrival in Harborview Station.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer told me he had it all figured out — when we get to Harborview Station, he's going to get a job because he doesn't think he's any good as a hustler or even as a bum, and I remember him asking me if that was okay.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne dies on the Fairview Plaza during the journey to Harborview Station, confirmed by Jesse Mercer and the Kendall Warren.
memories.memory_text: I died on the Fairview Plaza while we were heading to Harborview Station, and Jesse Mercer noticed something was wrong when he saw how stiff and still I was under the blanket.

grounded_facts: A Fairview Plaza journey from an unspecified location to Harborview Station, during which Sidney Thorne dies and Jesse Mercer reflects on his future.
memories.memory_text: I was on the Fairview Plaza with Jesse Mercer heading to Harborview Station, and I remember the Kendall Warren saying everything was fine, but I could tell something was wrong — I felt weak and couldn't move or speak, and I knew I wasn't going to make it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer, initially frightened, decides to comfort Sidney Thorne by putting his arm around him during the The First Trial.
Jesse Mercer reaches out and puts his arm around Sidney Thorne, a gesture of closeness or comfort.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer looking at me, then putting his arm around me on the Fairview Plaza — I could tell he was scared at first, but he still reached out to comfort me.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne derogatorily refers to Blair Hollis and others as 'faggots' in a stage whisper, showing prejudice and attempting to bond with Jesse Mercer through shared disdain.
memories.memory_text: I whispered to Jesse Mercer that there were more goddam faggots in this town, trying to show him I was on his side.

memories.memory_text: I was sitting in the booth when the TV showed a dating game contestant pick a suitor who turned out to be a dwarf, and everyone around me started laughing.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne tells Jesse Mercer that as a hustler, he needs management, suggesting he connect with Lane Finch named Alex Vaughn.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer he needs management as a hustler and suggested he connect with Alex Vaughn.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne introduce themselves and begin talking, leading to Jesse Mercer buying Sidney Thorne a drink and starting a conversation about Jesse Mercer's hustling.
memories.memory_text: I introduced myself to Jesse Mercer by saying my name is Sidney Thorne from the Bronx, and I started talking to him by complimenting his shirt; he bought me a drink, and I learned he's a hustler, which made me think I could connect with him over that.

grounded_facts: A daytime gathering at Everett's Bar where various marginal characters congregate, interact, and observe a TV game show.
memories.memory_text: I remember being at Everett's Bar during the day, where a bunch of us were hanging out, hiding from the daylight and watching a game show on TV while I grabbed a bottle and slid back into the booth.

grounded_facts: Blair Hollis sarcastically comments on Sidney Thorne's physical condition, implying he is small and weak, possibly disabled, in retaliation for Sidney Thorne's earlier insult.
memories.memory_text: Blair Hollis mocked me, saying he'd cut something out with his fingernail file and I wouldn't even need Blue Cross, like I'm some weak cripple.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer intervenes on Sidney Thorne's behalf when Blair Hollis mocks him, signaling growing solidarity between Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne.
memories.memory_text: I was mocked by Blair Hollis, and Jesse Mercer stepped in, saying 'Hey now, you heard him,' which made me realize he was standing up for me.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne runs into traffic, pretends to be hit by a taxi after slapping its fender, and collapses into Jesse Mercer's arms, causing the taxi to stop and traffic to halt.
memories.memory_text: I darted into traffic, slapped the taxi's fender, pretended to get hit, and fell into Jesse Mercer's arms so the cab would stop.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne yells obscenities at the cab Kendall Warren and later mocks him by biting his thumb after staging a fake accident.
memories.memory_text: I yelled at the cab Kendall Warren and later mocked him by biting my thumb after staging the fake accident.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne informs Jesse Mercer that with proper management, he could earn significantly more money by targeting wealthier, older female clients through a middleman like Alex Vaughn.
Sidney Thorne explains the market gap for older, wealthy women who need a middleman, positioning himself as Jesse Mercer's Jordan Marlowe and outlining a plan for higher earnings.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer it was a crime for a stud like him to only make twenty bucks a day when, with proper management and a middleman like Alex Vaughn, he could be taking home fifty or even a hundred a day by targeting older, wealthier women who can't come down to Times Square themselves.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne waves at the Bennett Keaton using a circle made with thumb and forefinger, which confuses the recipient.
memories.memory_text: I waved at the Bennett Keaton with my thumb and forefinger in a circle, and I could tell he was confused by it.

grounded_facts: A brief stop at a sidewalk cafe where Sidney Thorne spots and comments on a former client.
memories.memory_text: I remember stopping briefly at a sidewalk cafe where I spotted a former client and made a comment about him.

memories.memory_text: I pointed out that Bennett Keaton with the diamond cuff-links and told Jesse Mercer I'd placed him with Alex Vaughn just two weeks ago.
