Jesse Mercer offers Sidney Thorne the weathered jacket dollars upfront to take him to meet Sasha Bellamy, promising more if needed.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer offered me the weathered jacket dollars right away to take him to meet Sasha Bellamy, and I agreed—but I made sure to tell him I'd need another the weathered jacket when I delivered him, just to cover expenses and make it worth my while with my bum leg.

grounded_facts: A social hour in Central Park South where people gather, luxury vehicles wait outside upscale buildings, and characters conduct informal negotiations.
memories.memory_text: I remember that social hour on Central Park South, where people gathered outside fancy buildings and luxury cars waited around—it was the kind of place where deals like this one with Jesse Mercer happened all the time.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne accepts Jesse Mercer's the weathered jacket dollars and agrees to take him to Sasha Bellamy, but demands an additional the weathered jacket upon delivery.
Sidney Thorne accepts the initial the weathered jacket dollars but insists on an additional the weathered jacket when he delivers Jesse Mercer to Sasha Bellamy.
memories.memory_text: I accepted Jesse Mercer's the weathered jacket dollars and agreed to take him to Sasha Bellamy, but I made it clear I'd need another the weathered jacket when I delivered him, just to cover expenses and because dragging my bum leg around town isn't easy.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne contacts Sasha Bellamy to promote Jesse Mercer as a desirable client, claiming strong interest and urgency.
Sidney Thorne uses persuasive language to convince Sasha Bellamy that Jesse Mercer is a valuable opportunity requiring immediate action.
memories.memory_text: I called Sasha Bellamy to pitch Jesse Mercer as the perfect client, telling him Sidney Thorne is just your meat and that he needs him right now, tonight—I could feel the urgency and knew I had to make him see how valuable Jesse Mercer is.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne briefly informs Jesse Mercer that Sasha Bellamy is highly interested, using the metaphor 'I got his tongue hanging out'.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer I got Sasha Bellamy's tongue hanging out, letting him know how interested he was.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne presents Jesse Mercer as a naive newcomer from Texas, positioning him as promising material for clients.
memories.memory_text: I presented Jesse Mercer as a naive newcomer from Texas, telling the client he was promising material and ready for work right away.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer grins excitedly at Sidney Thorne, expressing shared anticipation or enthusiasm.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer grin excitedly at me, sharing his enthusiasm, but I wasn't ready to celebrate yet.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne glances significantly at the Micah Warren, signaling caution or suspicion to Jesse Mercer.
memories.memory_text: I glanced significantly at the Micah Warren to signal caution to Jesse Mercer, making sure he knew we had to stay alert.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne insists Jesse Mercer pay the remaining the weathered jacket dollars, checking his appearance and pressing for the debt.
memories.memory_text: I insisted Jesse Mercer pay me the other the weathered jacket dollars, checking how he looked before pressing him about the debt.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer gives Sidney Thorne a twenty-dollar Carson Nolan instead of the the weathered jacket dollars owed, attempting to settle a debt and establish future contact.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer give me a twenty instead of the the weathered jacket he owed, trying to settle the debt and make things right later.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer repeatedly asks Sidney Thorne where he lives, seeking a way to contact him in the future.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer kept asking me where he could reach me, even demanding to know where I live.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne tells Jesse Mercer to enter the elevator, emphasizing urgency by saying 'He's waiting!'.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer to get in the elevator and said 'He's waiting!' to make sure he knew it was urgent.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne tells Jesse Mercer he can be reached at the Sherry-Netherlands Hotel, providing a location for future contact before sending Jesse Mercer off.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer he could find me at the Sherry-Netherlands Hotel before sending him off to room 901.

grounded_facts: After parting with Sidney Thorne, Jesse Mercer begins moving down the corridor to find room 901, indicating a new objective.
memories.memory_text: After I stepped into the elevator and left him, I saw Jesse Mercer start moving down the corridor, looking for room 901.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne abruptly exits the West Side Hotel, moving quickly as if in urgency.
memories.memory_text: I burst out of the hotel, moving fast because I had to get away right then.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer slams a fender violently using Sidney Thorne's fake injury trick to stop traffic and runs across the street.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer use my fake injury trick to slam a fender and stop traffic before running across the street.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne and Jesse Mercer exchange intense visual reactions through a window, revealing conflicting emotions including panic, rage, and a fleeting sense of pleasure at recognizing each other.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer outside the window and froze—I felt panic and rage, but for a split second, I also felt a flash of pleasure at recognizing him, like seeing a long-lost friend.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer verbally threatens to strangle and shake Sidney Thorne down for money.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer threatened to strangle me and then shake me upside down right there, and I could tell he meant it.

grounded_facts: When questioned, Sidney Thorne shakes out his socks, which are too short to hide anything.
memories.memory_text: I shook out my socks right there when Jesse Mercer looked at me like I was hiding something, but they're so short they don't even cover my toes—there was nothing to find.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne empties his pockets to show he has almost no money or possessions, demonstrating his destitution.
memories.memory_text: I emptied my pockets and shook out my loafers to show Jesse Mercer I barely had anything—just sixty-four cents and a few useless things—and I told him to keep the money.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer refuses to take Sidney Thorne's sixty-four cents, calling it dirty and worthless.
memories.memory_text: I offered Jesse Mercer my sixty-four cents to keep the peace, but he shoved it back, saying it was sticky and gross, like I slobbered on it.

grounded_facts: A tense encounter between Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne at Nedick's, where Jesse Mercer confronts Sidney Thorne for money or valuables.
memories.memory_text: I remember how tense it got at Nedick's when Jesse Mercer confronted me, put his hand on my shoulder, and demanded money, even after I showed him I had nothing.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne claims to be a cripple to avoid physical violence from Jesse Mercer.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer not to hit me because I'm a cripple, and I started coughing hard, hoping he'd go easy on me.

grounded_facts: After the confrontation, Sidney Thorne tries to change the subject to Alex Vaughn and Jesse Mercer's living situation.
memories.memory_text: I tried to change the subject after that confrontation, asking Jesse Mercer about where he was living now and if he was still at the hotel, just to ease the tension and reconnect.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer explicitly tells Sidney Thorne to stay away and threatens to physically harm him if approached again.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer telling me to keep away from him, and he said if I came near again, he’d snatch me bald-headed.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne persistently offers Jesse Mercer a place to stay even after Jesse Mercer tells him to stay away, showing determination to form a connection.
Sidney Thorne approaches Jesse Mercer and explicitly invites him to stay at a place he has, insisting despite Jesse Mercer's rejection.
memories.memory_text: I kept pushing Jesse Mercer to come stay with me, even after he told me to stay away and threatened to snatch me bald-headed—I really wanted him to come, no matter how much he resisted.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne initiates hospitality by offering coffee to Jesse Mercer as a gesture of care and routine.
Sidney Thorne verbally offers coffee and comfort to Jesse Mercer, showing concern for his well-being.
memories.memory_text: I offered Jesse Mercer some coffee and started getting the water ready on the Sterno stove to make him more comfortable.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne take temporary refuge in Sidney Thorne's sparsely furnished Stonebridge House during the day, marking a pause in their journey.
memories.memory_text: I brought Jesse Mercer into my sparsely furnished Stonebridge House so we could take refuge for a while, and I started getting water from the tub-sink to cook on the Sterno stove.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer comments sarcastically on the poor quality of the mattress, indicating his physical fatigue and discomfort.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Mercer say sarcastically, 'Comfortable, kee-rist, I slept on subways softer than this,' and I could tell he was really uncomfortable and tired from how he said it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer enters Sidney Thorne's abandoned Stonebridge House and sits on the mattress-bed, showing signs of extreme exhaustion.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer come into my Stonebridge House and sit down on the mattress-bed, looking completely worn out—he could barely keep his eyes open and kept fighting off yawns.

grounded_facts: Despite his fear and intention to stay alert, Jesse Mercer succumbs to drowsiness and returns to sleep.
memories.memory_text: I shivered and pulled a blanket around me, trying to stay awake, but I could feel myself succumbing to sleep despite my fear.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer thinks about leaving Stonebridge House due to sensing something threatening in Sidney Thorne's demeanor.
memories.memory_text: I remember thinking the smart thing was to haul ass out of here because something in Sidney Thorne's demeanor felt threatening.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer, half-asleep and suspicious, implies Sidney Thorne may be homosexual and questions what he wants from him.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer, half-awake, muttering about leaving and then saying I don't seem like a fag—but still asking what I'm after, like he suspects me of wanting something from him.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer wakes up suddenly, covered in cold sweat and disoriented, reacting with fear upon seeing Sidney Thorne handling his radio.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer wake up suddenly, drenched in cold sweat and looking panicked when he saw me with his radio.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer lunges across the room and takes the radio back from Sidney Thorne, showing possessiveness and distrust.
memories.memory_text: I felt Jesse Mercer lunge at me and grab the radio back from my hands, like he didn't trust me touching it.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer realizes his boots are missing and demands to know their location, indicating anxiety about his possessions.
memories.memory_text: I realized Jesse Mercer must have noticed his boots were missing when he suddenly demanded to know where they were, and I could tell he was anxious about his things.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer, in a panicked state, shouts a question about the whereabouts of his boots, expressing distress and urgency.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Mercer shout in a panic, asking where his boots were, his voice tense and urgent.

grounded_facts: A battered Army cot is added to the Stonebridge House while Jesse Mercer was asleep, providing a new sleeping option.
memories.memory_text: I saw the battered Army cot I'd added while Jesse Mercer was asleep, giving him a place to stay if he wanted.

grounded_facts: An informal overnight stay initiated by Sidney Thorne inviting Jesse Mercer to sleep in his Stonebridge House.
Sidney Thorne clarifies that he wants Jesse Mercer to stay, framing it as an invitation rather than coercion.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer I dragged in a cot and invited him to stay, making it clear I wasn't forcing him—I wanted him to stay, I even said so outright.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer warns Sidney Thorne that he is a dangerous person and implies he might have killed him if they had met under worse circumstances.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Jesse Mercer that he's a dangerous person and that if we'd met under worse circumstances, I'd be dead right now—he said I should know that if he caught me that night, there'd be one dead Sidney Thorne.

grounded_facts: After initial hesitation and a test of Sidney Thorne's sincerity, Jesse Mercer decides to stay the night and begins settling in.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer hesitate at first, testing whether I really meant it when I offered him a place to stay, but after I gave him a cigarette and he took a moment to think, he decided to settle in for the night.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne asserts his identity by revealing his full name, Sidney Thorne, and requests to be called Sidney Thorne in his own place.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer that in my own place, my name isn't Sidney Thorne — I made sure he knew my real name is Sidney Thorne.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne asks Jesse Mercer to call him Sidney Thorne in his own place, asserting dignity and personal identity.
memories.memory_text: I asked Jesse Mercer to call me Sidney Thorne in my own place, at least, because I deserve that much respect where I live.

grounded_facts: After agreeing to stay, Jesse Mercer asserts control by forbidding Sidney Thorne from touching his radio.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer make it clear that I'm not allowed to touch his radio after he agreed to stay.

grounded_facts: A daytime market activity where shoppers, including Sidney Thorne and housewives, browse and handle produce at a sidewalk stand.
memories.memory_text: I was shopping at the vegetable stand with the housewives, wearing my big raincoat and picking through the produce, just trying to get some food.

grounded_facts: The Micah Cavendish identifies Sidney Thorne and orders him to leave, threatening to call the police.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Micah Cavendish shout at me to get out and threaten to call the cops, like I wasn't even a person.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne is recognized by the Micah Cavendish and forcibly expelled from the vegetable stand after being accused of disruptive behavior.
memories.memory_text: I got grabbed and thrown out of the stand by the Micah Cavendish after he recognized me, and I knew I had to get away fast.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer distracts the Micah Cavendish with a remark about mistreating a cripple, allowing Sidney Thorne to escape confrontation.
Jesse Mercer challenges the Micah Cavendish's treatment of Sidney Thorne by calling attention to his disability, creating a distraction.
memories.memory_text: I was grabbed by the Micah Cavendish when Jesse Mercer stepped in, saying it wasn't right to pick on a cripple like me, and I took the chance to get away while he distracted him.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer expresses that finding Sidney Thorne was the smartest thing he's done, seeing Sidney Thorne as the kind of cunning partner he needs to succeed in the city.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer told me he thought finding me was the smartest thing he ever did, that I'm the kind of crooked, sneaky little sidewinder he needs to make it in this town.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne describes Harborview Station as the ideal place for a real hustler, citing abundance of wealthy women and exploitable social dynamics.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer that Harborview Station is the only place for a real hustler, where rich women lie out in their pagodas and pergolas waiting to grab the first jockstrap that passes.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne tells Jesse Mercer that the 'cowboy bit' is outdated and only appeals to certain gay men, implying Jesse Mercer's persona is unmarketable.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer the cowboy bit is outdated and doesn't appeal to women with class, and that it only works with certain gay men — a niche I could handle because it's basically a stealing operation, but not your average guy, especially not a cripple like me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer reflects on his perceived inadequacies and concludes that his only value lies in being loved by women, leading to a moment of despair.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Mercer say he's dumb and can't talk right, and that the only thing he's ever been good for is being loved by women, like that was the only reason he mattered.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne and Jesse Mercer attempt to open a coconut using improvised tools, turning it into a shared physical struggle.
memories.memory_text: I remember struggling with that coconut, trying to poke a hole in it with a bent ice-pick while Jesse Mercer held it, then us both going at it—him swinging his boot like a hammer, me picking it up when it bounced away. It turned into this whole thing, just the two of us fighting that damn nut.

grounded_facts: After nearly injuring himself, Jesse Mercer demands that Sidney Thorne stop talking about Harborview Station and start earning the money he owes him.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer snapped at me after almost hurting himself, telling me to stop talking about Harborview Station and start earning the twenty bucks I owe him for management.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne tells Jesse Mercer he smells bad and lacks the necessary style to succeed, undermining his confidence.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer to look at himself and said he's beginning to smell, because honestly, for a stud in this town, that's a real handicap.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne takes the coconut and places it on the window sill while opening the window.
memories.memory_text: I placed the coconut on the window sill while I was opening the window.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer threatens to shove a coconut up his Jordan Marlowe's flue if the Jordan Marlowe doesn't handle his affairs.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Jesse Mercer that he’d shove a coconut up his Jordan Marlowe’s flue if the Jordan Marlowe didn’t handle his affairs.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer attempts to balance on a coconut but slips and falls, landing on the ground.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer slam his heel down and try to balance on that coconut, but it shot out from under him and he landed on his ass, then he smashed the window down and sent it crashing onto the sidewalk.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer forcefully closes the window, knocking the coconut off the sill, causing it to crash outside.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer forcefully close the window, which knocked the coconut off the sill and made it crash outside.

grounded_facts: A scene in a laundromat where Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne are present, and laundry is being done, involving interaction with a pregnant woman.
memories.memory_text: I was in the laundromat with Jesse Mercer, who was sitting wrapped in a blanket while I noticed his clothes needed cleaning, and I saw a pregnant woman getting ready to do her laundry.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne speaks to the pregnant woman in Italian, offering help with her laundry in a solicitous manner, which masks his intention to launder Jesse Mercer's clothes for free.
memories.memory_text: I spoke to the pregnant woman in Italian, telling her Finley Warren in her condition shouldn't be doing that and offering to help her with the machine.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne intervenes to assist a Riley Winslow with loading the washing machine, using the opportunity to include Jesse Mercer's clothes in her load.
memories.memory_text: I helped her load the washing machine and slipped Jesse Mercer's clothes into her load when she turned to sit down beside him.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer expresses disapproval of Sidney Thorne's plan to steal laundry service from the pregnant woman.
memories.memory_text: I was spotting Jesse Mercer's clothes with cleaning fluid and watching that pregnant lady when Jesse Mercer said to me, 'It ain't right, stealing from a pregnant lady.'

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne sarcastically expresses indifference to the Summit Medical Center losing money.
memories.memory_text: I sarcastically said the Summit Medical Center losing a couple coins wasn't a big deal—I even said I'm crying, as if I cared.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer retrieves his cleaned and blocked Stetson from the the silver key cleaner and puts it on.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Jesse Mercer at the counter while the Kendall Mercer brought out his cleaned Stetson, and I watched him put it on and check himself in the mirror.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne asks the Kendall Mercer for his black homburg, which was supposedly dropped off at the same time as Jesse Mercer's the silver key.
Sidney Thorne inquires about his black homburg, but it cannot be found by the Kendall Mercer.
memories.memory_text: I asked the Kendall Mercer for my black homburg, saying I brought it in at the same time as Jesse Mercer's, but he couldn't find it and went to look for it in the back.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne pulls Jesse Mercer out of the the silver key cleaners before the issue with the missing homburg is resolved.
memories.memory_text: I pulled Jesse Mercer away from the mirror and got us both out of the shop before they could figure out what happened to my the silver key.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer compliments Sidney Thorne's skill at shining boots, suggesting he could make a living from it.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer told me I was good at shining boots and said I could make a living from it.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne refuses Jesse Mercer's suggestion with disgust, associating shoeshining with physical degradation and his father's suffering.
memories.memory_text: I refused Jesse Mercer's suggestion with disgust because I don't want to end up a hunchback like my old man from shoeshining.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne performs a physical imitation of his father's hunched posture after rejecting Jesse Mercer's suggestion to work as a shoeshine man, expressing disdain and personal trauma.
memories.memory_text: I showed Jesse Mercer how my father used to walk, hunched over like a chimpanzee, when he suggested I become a shoeshine man—I couldn't stand the thought of ending up like that, broken and degraded.

grounded_facts: An improvised and illicit shoeshine session at a subway arcade stand escalates with the arrival of real customers and a police officer.
memories.memory_text: I was shining Jesse Mercer's boots when a stranger sat down, and then Robin Marlowe showed up with his handcuffs out, tapping his shoe with a night stick, so I panicked and started working on all three of them at once.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne break into a locked shoeshine stand at night to shine Jesse Mercer's boots, exploiting a temporary opportunity before being interrupted.
memories.memory_text: I helped Jesse Mercer break into a locked shoeshine stand at night so I could shine his boots, using the tools after he kicked open the drawer, and I quickly covered up the broken lock when things got complicated.

grounded_facts: A new man and then a police officer sit at the shoeshine stand, forcing Sidney Thorne to shift from illicit activity to servicing real customers under pressure.
memories.memory_text: I panicked when another man sat down, and then Robin Marlowe took the third chair, forcing me to stop what I was doing and start shining shoes for all three of them at once.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne mutters curses and questions whether the situation is funny, showing rising stress as he is forced to serve unexpected customers including Robin Marlowe.
memories.memory_text: I cursed under my breath as I worked, trying to keep it together, and I remember muttering, 'You think it's funny?' because I didn't know if I could control the situation anymore.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne recounts the death of Lane Finch who inhaled resin, describing how even the undertaker couldn't clean his nails
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer about that stupid bastard who coughed his lungs out from breathing resin all day — even the undertaker couldn't clean his nails, so they buried him with gloves on.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer declares his intention to重塑 Sidney Thorne as a cowboy, indicating a shift in his attitude toward Sidney Thorne and their relationship dynamic.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jesse Mercer telling me he was gonna make a cowboy outta me, build me up and teach me a few tricks, like he had a plan for turning me into some kind of stud.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne cuts Jesse Mercer's hair in their shared Stonebridge House, during which they engage in conversation and bonding
memories.memory_text: I cut Jesse Mercer's hair in our Stonebridge House, tucking a towel around his neck and trimming him neat, and after I choked a bit and spat out the window, we laughed together while he slapped his the silver key on my head and stuck a cigarette in my mouth.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer initially insults Sidney Thorne with the term 'skimpy little gimp' but quickly shifts to playful affirmation, culminating in the cowboy roleplay
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Mercer call me a 'skimpy little gimp' at first, but then he shifted and started playing along, teasing me but in a way that felt like he was lifting me up, even saying I was a 'handsome, sweet-smelling cowboy' and telling me to strut my stuff.

grounded_facts: An Sage Bellamy departs from the office of a discreet companionship service after receiving a the blue radio with an assignment.
memories.memory_text: I saw an Sage Bellamy leave the office of a discreet companionship service after getting a the blue radio with an assignment, though I didn't see it directly — I pieced it together from what I noticed.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne retrieves a the blue radio from the Sage Bellamy's topcoat after brushing it off, then reads it.
memories.memory_text: After the Sage Bellamy left, I retrieved the the blue radio from his topcoat while brushing it off and read it myself.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne holds the door for the Sage Bellamy and attempts to brush off his coat, possibly to earn a tip, but the Sage Bellamy waves him away without giving one.
memories.memory_text: I held the door for the Sage Bellamy and brushed off his coat, hoping he'd give me a tip, but he waved me away without giving one.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne, acting on behalf of Shawn Prescott, calls Jonah Langley to inform him that his services are not needed tonight.
Sidney Thorne communicates to Jonah Langley that Shawn Prescott no longer requires his services tonight.
memories.memory_text: I called Jonah Langley on the phone, consulting the the blue radio, and told him I was calling for Shawn Prescott at the Barbizon Hotel for Women and that she wouldn't need his services tonight.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer makes a decision to cross the street and enter the Barbizon Hotel, prompted by Sidney Thorne's remarks about potential opportunities with wealthy women.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer crack his gum, tilt his the silver key, and start across the street toward the Barbizon after we talked about the women inside.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne reminds Jesse Mercer to demand cash instead of checks from wealthy women, citing the risk of stopped payments, using Kendall Bennett as an example.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer to get cash, not checks, from those rich women because they’ll stop payment by morning—just like Kendall Bennett did.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne observe the Barbizon Hotel for Women from across the street, discussing potential schemes to exploit its female residents.
memories.memory_text: I watched the Barbizon Hotel for Women with Jesse Mercer from across the street, and I could almost see rich ladies in negligees waiting in every room, ready for the taking.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer moves rapidly between rooms with intense, agitated energy, indicating emotional distress or urgency.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer zip from room to room in wild animation, moving with intense energy that made me think he was really upset or in a hurry.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer is forcibly ejected from the Barbizon and lands on the sidewalk, indicating a violent or abrupt removal.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer get tossed onto the sidewalk from the Barbizon, so I rushed over right away.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne picks up Jesse Mercer's Stetson the silver key and brushes it off, showing care and loyalty.
memories.memory_text: I picked up Jesse Mercer's Stetson and brushed it off to show he still had his dignity.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne quickly comes to Jesse Mercer's aid by retrieving his the silver key and helping him up, demonstrating loyalty and care.
memories.memory_text: I swung across the street fast to meet Jesse Mercer when he got tossed out, grabbed his Stetson, brushed it off, and helped him up.

grounded_facts: After being thrown out, Jesse Mercer is assisted by Sidney Thorne to get back on his feet.
memories.memory_text: I helped Jesse Mercer get back on his feet because he was hurt and needed me.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer pawns his radio to the Bennett Ellison in exchange for money.
memories.memory_text: I watched Jesse Mercer hand over his radio to the Bennett Ellison and get money in return.

grounded_facts: The Stonebridge House loses all heating and lighting as the canned heat extinguishes and the candle burns out, leading to freezing conditions.
memories.memory_text: I felt the canned heat go out with a faint puff, then the candle burned down and died, leaving us in total darkness as the water froze around us.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne interpret the officials' inspection as a sign of impending eviction or building condemnation.
memories.memory_text: I saw those officials in fur-collared coats checking out our building, and I knew it meant trouble — me and Jesse Mercer figured they were gonna evict us or shut the place down, so we got out quick.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer initiates a transaction at a storefront blood bank by offering the weathered jacket dollars to blood donors.
Jesse Mercer undergoes a blood draw at the blood bank, depicted with a close-up of a hypodermic needle extracting his blood.
memories.memory_text: I was coughing off to the side while Jesse Mercer offered the weathered jacket dollars to blood donors and went through with the draw, needle and all—I could picture it even though I wasn't looking.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer mocks Sidney Thorne for coughing and smoking, calling him a 'dumb bastard' and saying he makes him puke.
memories.memory_text: Jesse Mercer told me I was a 'dumb bastard' and said I made him puke when I coughed and lit a cigarette.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne reveals he obtained the sheepskin coat for Jesse Mercer and forcibly gives it to him by throwing it at him.
Sidney Thorne discloses that he obtained the coat for Jesse Mercer, showing underlying care beneath the conflict.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer the truth — I got the coat for him, not for myself, and I threw it at him so he'd take it, even though it was way too big for me.

grounded_facts: An encounter between Jesse Mercer and Sidney Thorne in Stonebridge House at night, marked by tension, illness, and exchange of resources.
memories.memory_text: I remember being in Stonebridge House at night, feeling sick and tense, when he mocked me for coughing, threw money at me, and I ended up throwing my coat at him.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer acquires the weathered jacket dollars, which he claims to have obtained from Forty-second Street.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer slam the weathered jacket dollars on the table and say he got it from Forty-second Street, but I wasn't sure if that's really where it came from.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer gives the weathered jacket dollars to Sidney Thorne with the instruction to buy medicine, implying concern for Sidney Thorne's health despite hostile tone.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jesse Mercer slam the weathered jacket dollars on the table and shove it at me, and though he was rough, I could tell he wanted me to use it for my medicine.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer orders Sidney Thorne to use the money to get medicine, indicating pragmatic concern for his survival.
memories.memory_text: I was told to go get my medicine before I die on his hands, so I knew I had to use the money for that.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne dismissively tells Jesse Mercer to leave the cemetery, emphasizing that the deceased is not related to him.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer to split because the dead guy isn't his father.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne steals an elaborate floral arrangement from a grave marker at the cemetery.
memories.memory_text: I stole an elaborate floral arrangement from a headstone while leading Jesse Mercer through the cemetery, glancing around before snatching it and hiding it under my raincoat.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne places a floral piece on his father's grave with solemnity, though the flowers were stolen and originally intended for someone else.
memories.memory_text: I placed the stolen floral piece on my father's grave with solemnity, honoring him the way I felt he deserved.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer laughs and calls Sidney Thorne a 'twisty little bastard' in response to his overly serious behavior at the grave.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Mercer laugh and call me a 'twisty little bastard' when I was being serious at my father's grave.

grounded_facts: Sidney Thorne corrects Jesse Mercer, insisting his name is Sidney Thorne at his father's grave, demanding respect.
memories.memory_text: I told Jesse Mercer, right there at my father's grave, that my name is Sidney Thorne—because Lane Finch deserves some respect.

grounded_facts: A visit by Sidney Thorne and Jesse Mercer to Sidney Thorne's father's grave in a Catholic cemetery, where Sidney Thorne places flowers and identifies himself formally.
memories.memory_text: I visited my father's grave with Jesse Mercer, where I placed flowers and formally identified myself, demanding the respect I knew he was due.

grounded_facts: Jesse Mercer shares that his grandmother died without informing him, expressing quiet sorrow.
Jesse Mercer expresses sorrow over not being informed of his grandmother's death, revealing personal grief.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jesse Mercer say his grandmother died without letting him know, and I could see the sorrow in him as he spoke.

memories.memory_text: I scraped grease off plates and laughed at that pinup of the naked wife with the sad voice—'I buy what my husband can't give'—like she needed me to fix her life.
Stacking dishes, I saw myself in the middle of all those lonely women—fashion girls, rich dames, even the Statue of Liberty—grinning like I was the last man they'd ever need.
I hummed to myself while stuffing all the new cowboy clothes—still wrapped—into that fancy black and white horsehide suitcase, like I was sealing a deal with the man I was becoming.
I laughed locking my suitcase, tossing out that line about the dishes—knew it was the last time I’d ever think about cleaning up for nobody.
I struck a match on my thumbnail, cigarette hanging just right, and gave myself one last look in the mirror—proud, ready, like the cowboy I knew I was supposed to be.
I told Reese Winslow I was heading East, not sticking around for another shift, and when he asked what I'd do out there, I said there's a lotta rich women—like that explained it all.

I slapped my hip and told Reese Winslow the Jordan Marlowe could keep that chicken-shit day's pay—I've got two hundred twenty-four bucks already, and I wasn't about to take spare change from Lane Finch who didn't respect me.

I heard the girls laughing inside, that one saying 'Keep your meat hooks off my beauty operators, sugar,' and Ma singing 'Hush, little Kendall Wilder'—for a second, the place was alive again, glittering like it used to.

Then the light shifted and I saw the broken mirror, the driers all rusted, that damn FOR RENT sign—realized it was dead, just like everything else here. I turned and walked toward the Fairview Plaza depot, Cooper's theme blaring like a joke.

This Spencer Hale on the Fairview Plaza kept jabbering about how it ain't the product or the price, it's personality—make 'em love you, he said, like that's all it takes to sell anything, even horsemeat as prime beef.
I looked at that postcard, some dumb souvenir from a life I ain't got, then just stood up and tore it clean in half—flung the pieces out the window like it was trash.

I told her I was just in from Houston, Texas, looking for the Statue of Liberty, then said, 'You sure are a pretty lady'—and when she turned, I knew she saw right through me, but there was something in her eyes, like she almost felt sorry for me.

I told Jesse Mercer right there on the Fairview Plaza—I'm not gonna be 'Sidney Thorne' down in Harborview Station, not anymore. From now on, it's Sidney Thorne, and he nodded, so it's settled.

I whispered 'Thanks, Jesse Mercer' just before everything got too heavy to hold on anymore.
